To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the driving force of homo-chiral complex formation in chiral systems is the effort of the systems to separate the most symmetrical associates from the less symmetrical ones, while the driving force for heterochiral complexation is the effort to separate the least symmetrical associates from more symmetrical ones.

the driving force of diastereomer separation is the effort of the mixture to achieve the highest possible symmetry of the system; the outcome of the separation is encoded in the structure of the compounds; the outcome of separation is modified by the intervention kinetic control.

the efficiency of resolution can be predicted by the use of the same parameters as are used in the case of enantiomers and, moreover, the efficiency of resolution is a function of the structure of the compounds involved.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prediction of diastereoselection in the resolution of racemic compounds by means of chiral resolving agents.
the prediction of the behaviour of diastereomeric mixtures, and thus with the prediction of resolution efficiency.
the prediction of the efficiency of separation of diastereomeric compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structure of a chiral compound is responsible for the result of the optical resolution.
the behaviour of enantio- and diastereoisomeric mixtures is similar, although the outcome of the process is different.
the driving force of chiral recognition is symmetry, and the driving force of diastereomer separation is the pursuit of symmetry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the resolution of diastereomers is the result of the interaction between the chiral compounds.
the behaviour of enantio- and diastereomeric mixtures in liquid and solid phases is similar.
in the case of enantiomer separation the driving force is symmetry, while in case of diastereomer separation it is a kind of symmetry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the driving force of diastereomer separation in chiral compounds is probably the effort of the (mixture of) compounds to achieve the most symmetric distribution of associates.
the behaviour of diastereomers in the presence of a chiral resolving agent is similar to the behaviour of enantio- and diastereomers.
the driving force of the separation of diastereomers can be understood in terms of symmetry, as is the case with the separation of enantiomers.
